findings.body: After the answer query has returned its contributing `activeBatchIds`, this performs a separate lookup of whatever batches are active now and replaces those executed pins wholesale. If a reload activates batch B between the answer query and this call, the displayed result came from batch A while names and summaries use B. When both batches have the same total but different lines, the signed link is drillable and opens B's transactions rather than the transactions behind the displayed answer; when totals differ, a valid row is incorrectly made inert. Collect the complete window pins from the same execution snapshot, or fail closed when this lookup disagrees with the contributing pins.
findings.title: Pin collection can switch the answer to a post-query reload

findings.body: This new repository operation is not called anywhere in `drill-transactions.repository.test.ts`; the sparse-window tests substitute `FakeTransactions.findActiveActualPins`, so they cannot detect an incorrect active-only filter, range bound, row conversion, or ordering in this SQL. The task explicitly requires that repository test file to be added or changed, but it remains unchanged. Add an owner-boundary test that exercises this method and verifies the returned pins and query constraints.

findings.body: The added size-limit rule says an oversized row carries no amount, but the generic context description at lines 82–84 still says every row binds its exact-paise Actual, and C5a at lines 223–224 repeats that each row carries one. These requirements remain mutually exclusive despite the implementation's discriminated union. Explicitly exempt the C5d inert variant in both generic descriptions.
